rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`. The requirement has one obligation for each site: the description MUST state when to use the skill in terms of the user's task.

The front-matter `description` does this. It says to use the skill "at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas". It then gives concrete signs of such a project: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the mdBook, or `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code. That is a condition on the user's task and project, not a description of the skill's internals. It also names the other bundled skills to pick for particular tasks: habeas-requirements, habeas-refactor, habeas-evidence and habeas-bootstrap-requirements. The requirement allows this with MAY, and it helps an agent avoid confusing the skills. The trailing sentence about directive syntax, `habeas status` and `habeas info`, and gotchas adds reference scope but does not weaken the when-to-use statement.

No violation queries were listed for this site, so no violation matches needed judging. I found no gap.
